subject: Error: No acceptably small step size could be found. Perhaps the posterior is not continuous?

messages.author: 6ad178c9bfa534b7
messages.subject: Error: No acceptably small step size could be found. Perhaps the posterior is not continuous?
parts:
This error is being discussed on the developer's list (https://groups.google.com/d/topic/stan-dev/y0O5gUVaOtY/discussion)

Error in sampler$call_sampler(args_list[[i]]) : 
  No acceptably small step size could be found. Perhaps the posterior is not continuous?

I've also had this error when I've used a uniform distribution as a prior for a scale parameter, and (1)  did not add an upper bound to the scale parameter that
matches the uniform distribution and (2) did not set the maximum of the uniform distribution high enough that it is not encountered in sampling. 

The example of a local level DLM that I paste below has this error. In this example, it is my fault for setting the upper bound on the prior too low. And since I am just using the uniform distribution as a proper uninformative prior, it is easy enough to change.  However, the inability to set bounds on arrays or vectors makes is a pain to try to use uniform distributions (or any truncated distribution) as hard constraints if there are different bounds for different elements.  

Example code (data and initialization data attached).

dlm_code <- 'data {
     // number of obs
     int<lower=1> n_obs;
     // total time periods
     int<lower=1> n_total;
     // observed data
     real y[n_obs];
     // time of each obs
     int<lower=1,upper=n_total> y_time[n_obs];
     // priors
     real theta0_mean;
     real<lower=0.0> theta0_sd;
     real<lower=0.0> sigma_theta_max;
     real<lower=0.0> sigma_y_max;
}
parameters {
     // Measurement error
     real<lower=0.0> sigma_y;
     // real<lower=0.0,upper=sigma_y_max> sigma_y;
     // system error
     real<lower=0.0> sigma_theta;
     // real<lower=0.0,upper=sigma_theta_max> sigma_theta;
     // latent states
     real theta[n_total + 1];
}
model {
      for (i in 1:n_obs) {
       y[i] ~ normal(theta[y_time[i] + 1], sigma_y);
      }
      theta[1] ~ normal(theta0_mean, theta0_sd);
      for (i in 2:(n_total + 1)) {
            theta[i] ~ normal(theta[i - 1], sigma_theta);
      }
      sigma_theta ~ uniform(0.0, sigma_theta_max);
      sigma_y ~ uniform(0.0, sigma_y_max);
}
'

library (rstan)
source_env <- function(file, ..., env.opts = list(parent=parent.frame()) ) {
    e <- do.call(new.env, env.opts)
    sys.source(file, envir=e, ...)
    e
}
model_data <- as.list(source_env("data.R"))
model_init <- list(as.list(source_env("init_1.R")))
dlm_fit <- stan(model_code = dlm_code, data = model_data, init = model_init,
                     iter = 10, n_chains = 1)
## Produces the error:
## Error in sampler$call_sampler(args_list[[i]]) : 
     ##  No acceptably small step size could be found. Perhaps the posterior is not continuous? 

## No error if I either
## 1. add upper bounds to sigma_y and sigma_theta
## or
## 2. increase sigma_y_max and sigma_theta_max so that the boundary
## is not hit.
model_data_2 <- within(model_data, {
    sigma_y_max <- sigma_y_max * 100
    sigma_theta_max <- sigma_theta_max * 100
})
dlm_fit_2 <- stan(model_code = dlm_code, data = model_data_2, init = model_init,
                     iter = 10, n_chains = 1)

parts:
@Jeffrey, I don't completely understand your solution to the "No acceptably small step size could be found."-problem and I don't understand why it occurs.

I can get the same error with a much more simple model:

library(rstan)
seed <- 12345
set.seed(seed)
norm_data <- rnorm(100, mean=5, sd=1)

norm_model1 <- '
  data {
    int<lower=1> n;
    real norm_data[n];
  }

  parameters {
    real m;
    real<lower=0> sd;
  }

  model {
    sd ~ uniform(1, 10);
    m ~ uniform(1, 10);
    norm_data ~ normal(m, sd);
  }
'

data_list <- list(norm_data=norm_data, n=length(norm_data))

stan(model_code = norm_model1, data = data_list, iter = 10, chains = 2, seed = seed)

##
## TRANSLATING MODEL 'norm_model1' FROM Stan CODE TO C++ CODE NOW.
## COMPILING THE C++ CODE FOR MODEL 'norm_model1' NOW.
## SAMPLING FOR MODEL 'norm_model1' NOW (CHAIN 1).

## Error: No acceptably small step size could be found. Perhaps the posterior
## is not continuous?




While if I just change the prior of the mean from uniform(1, 10) to uniform(-10, 10) the error goes away.

norm_model2 <- '
  data {
    int<lower=1> n;
    real norm_data[n];
  }

  parameters {
    real m;
    real<lower=0> sd;
  }

  model {
    sd ~ uniform(1, 10);
    m ~ uniform(-10, 10);
    for(i in 1:n) {
      norm_data[i] ~ normal(m, sd);
    }
  }
'

stan(model_code = norm_model2, data = data_list, iter = 10000, chains = 2, seed = seed)


##
## TRANSLATING MODEL 'norm_model2' FROM Stan CODE TO C++ CODE NOW.
## COMPILING THE C++ CODE FOR MODEL 'norm_model2' NOW.
## SAMPLING FOR MODEL 'norm_model2' NOW (CHAIN 1).
## Iteration:    1 / 10000 [  0%]  (Adapting)
## Iteration: 1000 / 10000 [ 10%]  (Adapting)
## Iteration: 2000 / 10000 [ 20%]  (Adapting)
# etc...




When building a model I find it quite convenient to start out using uniform priors and later change them to better suited priors. However, I seem to encounter the "No acceptably small step size could be found."-problem a lot when using uniform priors. Any thought on what the problem could be and how to solve it?

/Rasmus

(Self contained code to replicate the error and sessionInfo is attached.)

messages.author: 2a7f346506a3e9ff
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Re: Error: No acceptably small step size could be found. Perhaps the posterior is not continuous?
parts:
This error is due, in part, to a bug in stan which has been recently fixed.  The next release will help a little.  More generally though this error will come up if your variables can be initialized outside the support of your distribution.  It is crucial that if you use Uniform priors that your constrain the relevant parameters to lie in the appropriate range.  Not doing this can lead to errors like this as well as poor sampling.

Cheers,
Marcus
